blocks.html: From a homestay in Wayanad to a jewellery showroom in Thrissur, customers here open WhatsApp before they open anything else — yet most small teams still juggle those chats on a single phone that never stops buzzing. The WhatsApp Business API changes the maths: one verified number, a shared inbox for the whole team, automated replies that never sleep, and broadcasts that land in the app people actually check.

This guide walks a growing business through everything the platform can do — a shared team inbox, WhatsApp broadcasting, chatbot automation, in-chat commerce, ads that start a conversation, and the CRM links that tie it together — plus what it costs and how to get approved. Ojiva AI runs all of it on one dashboard alongside Bulk SMS and RCS, so book a free demo and we'll map it against how your own team already handles enquiries.

sections.heading: How WhatsApp Business API Pricing Actually Works

blocks.html: There are only two parts to the cost, and understanding them prevents nasty surprises. The first is Meta's own messaging charge; the second is the platform fee from your provider. Meta bills per delivered message rather than by the old 24-hour conversation, and what you pay tracks how much you send.

items.title: Two parts to the cost:
items.desc: Meta's per-message charge plus your provider's platform fee — nothing hidden beyond that.

items.title: Charged per template, by category:
items.desc: marketing, utility and authentication templates are each priced differently.

items.title: Replies are usually free:
items.desc: answering a customer who messaged first, inside the service window, generally carries no charge.

items.title: Volume shapes the bill:
items.desc: per-message pricing means the cost follows your sending, not a flat per-conversation rate.

blocks.html: Because the exact rate depends on the message category and the customer's country, the honest answer to "what will it cost" is a short calculation against your real volumes rather than a headline number. The official breakdown lives in Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform pricing documentation, and Ojiva AI will size it against your own campaigns during setup.

sections.heading: Getting Set Up: Approval, Templates and the DLT Question

blocks.html: Getting live is a dashboard workflow, not a developer project. You need a verified Meta Business account, a phone number that isn't currently active on the consumer WhatsApp or Business app, a display name, and a set of message templates for Meta to review before your first send.
It is also worth clearing up the most common mix-up in India, because it trips up almost every business coming from text campaigns: WhatsApp does not use the SMS registration path.

items.title: Verify the business:
items.desc: a Meta Business account and a dedicated number get the process moving.

items.title: Get the name and templates approved:
items.desc: Meta reviews your display name and message templates before anything goes out.

items.title: Set consent and opt-out:
items.desc: follow DPDP Act principles — a clear opt-in at capture and an easy way out.

items.title: Go live and measure:
items.desc: broadcasts, automations and reporting all run from the first day.

blocks.html: To settle the question directly: DLT registration is a TRAI mechanism specific to SMS, and it does not apply to WhatsApp. The API uses Meta's own Business verification and template-review system instead, which is what produces your verified badge. Consent still matters and should follow DPDP Act principles, but the SMS DLT process is a separate track. Ojiva AI handles the verification and template review for you, and the specifics are set out in Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform documentation.

items.q: How does the WhatsApp Business API work for a business in Kerala?
items.a: It upgrades an ordinary WhatsApp number into a multi-agent, automated channel. A provider like Ojiva AI onboards the business, gets it verified and its templates approved, and then you run a shared inbox, broadcasts, a chatbot and integrations from one dashboard — all on the app your customers already use every day.

items.q: How much does the WhatsApp Business API cost for a small business?
items.a: There are two parts: Meta's per-message charge, which varies by message category, and the platform fee from your provider. There is no per-conversation fee — you pay for what you send — and replies to a customer who messaged first are generally free within the service window. The right figure comes from a quick calculation against your real volumes.

items.q: What do you need to get approved for the WhatsApp Business API?
items.a: A verified Meta Business account, a phone number not currently active on the consumer WhatsApp or Business app, a display name, and message templates for Meta's review. A provider handles most of the paperwork and the review process, so the business isn't left decoding Meta's requirements alone.

items.q: Can a business message customers in Malayalam on WhatsApp?
items.a: Yes. Replies and approved templates can be written in Malayalam, English or both, in the same thread. It is a practical way to serve customers who are more comfortable in the local language, and it tends to lift both trust and response rates.

items.q: How can hotels and travel agencies in Kerala use the WhatsApp Business API?
items.a: They can manage booking enquiries, send confirmations and check-in reminders, and let a chatbot answer routine questions around the clock, with complex requests passed to a human through the shared inbox. For a tourism business fielding enquiries at all hours, that combination of instant answers and a clean handoff is the main draw.

items.q: Does the WhatsApp Business API connect with a CRM or online store?
items.a: Yes. It integrates with CRMs and stores such as WooCommerce, Shopify and Zoho, so leads sync automatically, records update themselves, and events like a new order or an abandoned cart can trigger the right message without manual work.

items.q: Is the WhatsApp Business API billed per message or per conversation?
items.a: Per message. Meta now charges when a template message is delivered rather than by the old 24-hour conversation, with rates set by category — marketing, utility or authentication. Non-template replies sent within an open customer service window are generally free, so answering an existing customer usually carries no charge.

items.q: Is DLT registration needed to send WhatsApp business messages in India?
items.a: No. DLT registration is a TRAI process specific to SMS. WhatsApp uses Meta's own Business verification and template-review system instead, so the SMS DLT track does not apply. Consent and opt-out still matter and should follow DPDP Act principles, but that is separate from DLT.
